label: D2 after a common a1 -> S1 transition (fades late in the episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 steps whose inputs are last action a1 and state S1, i.e. the agent chose a1 and got the common transition to S1. It never fires at D1 or GO, and never on a1 -> S2 (rare), a2 -> S2, or a2 -> S1. (phase==D2)&(action==1)&(state==1) alone gets recall 1.0 and precision 0.78. The misses come from episode time: the activation drifts down across the episode and goes to zero after about trial 75-80, so adding ep_trial<80 gives dev F1 0.98. Both action and state are observed at D2, so this uses no future variables. Magnitude, from the example windows only: it is near max when the previous trial was rewarded and a1 -> S1 has been repeated, about 0.87 when the D1 reward input was 0, and it shrinks steadily with episode trial. Activation mass is concentrated where the model value is high (top value bin 74%).

issues: Every factual claim checks out on the test split. phase != D2 has recall 0, so the feature never fires at D1 or GO. D2 steps other than a1 -> S1 have recall 1.9e-5 and mass recall 1.5e-7. D2 & a1 & S1 without the time cutoff gives recall 1.0 and precision 0.78. Adding ep_trial<80 gives F1 0.981.

The remaining false positives are not noise: they sit in the fade window. With ep_trial<70 precision is 0.999. In the band 70 <= ep_trial < 80 precision is only 0.72. So the cutoff at trial 80 is a rough threshold on a gradual decline, which the label already reflects with 'fades late'. A threshold sweep on test gives F1 0.947 at 70, 0.979 at 75, 0.986 at 78, 0.981 at 80 and 0.969 at 82, so trial 78 is a tiny improvement that is not material.
Misses on test are 154 steps holding 0.0% of the activation mass. They are all tiny activations at D2 a1 -> S1 steps, so they are scattered and not systematic.

No future variables are used: action and state are observed at D2 (as in_action and in_state). The magnitude claims about reward and repetition were not checked in detail. They are secondary and are framed as coming from the example windows only.
